answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The result is a self-purifying economy: every epoch, low-cost fake identities are filtered out by the same reputation mechanics that reward the honest ones. Consider a jetty as the anchor of the cost. A forge stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a dawn...
